 EXHIBIT 99.1

 

 

Apyx Medical Corporation Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

 

    •   Reported total revenue of $14.0 million in the third quarter of 2026 primarily driven by 17% growth in the Surgical Aesthetics segment
    •   Initiated successful full commercial launch of the power liposuction handpiece for the AYON system in the third quarter
    •   Reaffirmed total revenue guidance for FY2026 of $59.0 million to $60.0 million
    •   Management to host a conference call today at 8:00 a.m. ET

 

CLEARWATER, FL — November 5, 2026 - Apyx Medical Corporation (NASDAQ:APYX) (“Apyx Medical;” the “Company”), the leader in surgical aesthetics marketed and sold as Renuvion® and the AYON Body Contouring System™ (AYON), today reported financial results for its third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

 

Recent Financial and Operating Highlights:

 

•

Reported total revenue of $14.0 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with $12.9 million in the same period last year.
 

◦

Surgical Aesthetics revenue increased to $13.0 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with $11.1 million in the third quarter of 2025, which was the result of sales of AYON domestically and Renuvion generators internationally. 
  ◦ OEM revenue was approximately $1.1 million in the third quarter of 2026, representing a decrease of 42% from the same period last year.
  • Net loss attributable to stockholders of $1.8 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with a net loss attributable to stockholders of $2.0 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Adjusted EBITDA was $0.4 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared with Adjusted EBITDA loss of $0.1 million for the third quarter of 2025.
  • Initiated the full commercial launch of the reusable power liposuction handpiece for the AYON Body Contouring System in the third quarter of 2026, following positive feedback from key early adopter surgeons.
  • Published prospective clinical study supporting Renuvion’s effects on biological markers associated with skin quality in the peer-reviewed academic journal Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery—Global Open. Among six participants completing six-month follow-up, treated tissue demonstrated 30% greater elastin fiber density and 34% less inflammation compared with untreated control areas.

 

“We are pleased to report 17% growth in our Surgical Aesthetics business for the quarter, reflecting continued adoption of AYON and the progress we are making in executing our commercial strategy,” said Charlie Goodwin, President and Chief Executive Officer. “Over the past year, we have continued to demonstrate the value AYON offers by providing a full suite of complementary body contouring capabilities in one integrated platform. We are building on that foundation with the broader commercial launch of power liposuction, which has received very positive early feedback from surgeons since it received FDA clearance earlier this year. We estimate that approximately 70% of plastic surgeons use power liposuction, making this an important addition that broadens AYON’s appeal.”

Third Quarter 2026 Results:

 

Total revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026, increased 9% to $14.0 million, compared with $12.9 million in the prior year period. Surgical Aesthetics segment sales increased 17%, or $1.9 million, to approximately $13.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, when compared with $11.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The Surgical Aesthetics sales increase was driven by sales of AYON, which commenced with the commercial launch in the third quarter of 2025 and increased sales of generators internationally. These increases were partially offset by decreases in domestic sales of standalone generators and single-use handpieces globally. OEM segment sales decreased 42%, or $0.8 million, to approximately $1.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 when compared with $1.8 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease in OEM sales was due to a decrease in sales volume to existing customers. With the increased focus on Surgical Aesthetics, the Company expects that OEM segment revenue will decrease for the year.

 

Gross profit for the three months ended September 30, 2026, increased 8% to $9.0 million, compared with $8.3 million for the same period in the prior year. Gross margin for the three months ended September 30, 2026, was relatively steady at 64.2%, compared to 64.4% for the same period in 2025. 

 

 

2
 

Operating expenses increased to $9.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared with $9.1 million for the same period last year. The increase in operating expenses was driven by a $0.4 million increase in salaries and related costs and a $0.2 million increase in selling, general and administrative expenses, partially offset by a $0.2 million decrease in professional services.

 

Other expense, net increased slightly to $1.1 million for each of the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared with $1.0 million for the same period last year.

 

Net loss attributable to stockholders was $1.8 million, or $0.04 per share, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared with $2.0 million, or $0.05 per share, in the prior year period.

 

Adjusted EBITDA for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $0.4 million as compared with an Adjusted EBITDA loss of $0.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

 

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, net cash used in operating activities was $1.6 million, compared with $3.5 million used in the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease was primarily due to changes in working capital combined with a reduction in net loss. As of September 30, 2026, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $25.8 million. 

 

Financial Guidance for Full Year 2026:

 

The Company reaffirmed its revenue guidance targets and updated its operating expenses target for the year ending December 31, 2026:

 

 

•

Total revenue in the range of $59.0 million to $60.0 million, compared with $52.8 million reported for the year ended December 31, 2025.
 

◦

Total revenue guidance assumes:
 

▪

Surgical Aesthetics revenue is expected to be in the range of $54.0 million to $55.0 million, compared with approximately $45.3 million reported for the year ended December 31, 2025.
 

▪

OEM revenue is expected to be approximately $5.0 million, compared with approximately $7.5 million for the year ended December 31, 2025.
  • The Company expects gross margins in the range of 63% to 65%.
  • Total Company now expects operating expenses in the range of $41.0 million to $42.5 million for the year ended December 31, 2026, down from the previous guidance of less than $45.0 million.

About AYON Body Contouring System™:

AYON is a groundbreaking, surgeon-designed body contouring system that combines precision, versatility, and innovation in an all-in-one platform. It seamlessly integrates advanced fat removal technologies, Renuvion’s tissue contraction and electrosurgical capabilities, empowering surgeons to deliver the most comprehensive body contouring treatments for patients. With advanced features like LIFT Technology for real-time adjustments and Renuvion for enhanced tissue contraction, AYON sets a new standard in surgical care, streamlining procedures and maximizing patient outcomes. Backed by Apyx Medical’s expertise and evidence-based design, AYON delivers consistent, reliable performance and an unmatched return on investment. As the first of its kind, AYON is revolutionizing body contouring and shaping the future of aesthetic surgery.

 

About Apyx Medical Corporation:

 

Apyx Medical Corporation is a surgical aesthetics company with a passion for elevating people’s lives through innovative products, including its Helium Plasma Platform Technology products marketed and sold as Renuvion® and the AYON Body Contouring SystemTM in the cosmetic surgery market and J-Plasma® in the hospital surgical market. Renuvion and J-Plasma offer surgeons a unique ability to provide controlled heat to tissue to achieve their desired results. The effectiveness of Renuvion and J-Plasma are supported by more than 90 clinical documents. 
The AYON Body Contouring System is an FDA-cleared, groundbreaking, surgeon-designed body contouring system that combines precision, versatility, and innovation in an all-in-one platform. It seamlessly integrates fat removal, closed loop contouring, electrosurgical capabilities and Renuvion for tissue contraction, empowering surgeons to deliver the most comprehensive body contouring treatments for patients. 
The Company also leverages its deep expertise and decades of experience in unique waveforms through OEM agreements with other medical device manufacturers. For further information about the Company and its products, please refer to the Apyx Medical Corporation website at 


www.ApyxMedical.com.

Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measure

 

The Company has presented the following non-GAAP financial measure in this press release: adjusted EBITDA. The Company defines adjusted EBITDA as its reported net income (loss) attributable to stockholders (GAAP) plus income tax expense (benefit), interest, depreciation and amortization, stock-based compensation expense and other significant non-recurring items.

 

We present the following non-GAAP measure because we believe such measure is a useful indicator of our operating performance. Our management uses this non-GAAP measure principally as a measure of our operating performance and believes that this measure is useful to investors because it is frequently used by analysts, investors and other interested parties to evaluate companies in our industry. We also believe that this measure is useful to our management and investors as a measure of comparative operating performance from period to period. The non-GAAP financial measure presented in this release should not be considered as a substitute for, or preferable to, the measures of financial performance prepared in accordance with GAAP.
